newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease, still depressed by IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease, still depressed by IMF news.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds fell on Friday in trading overshadowed mainly by Thursday's news the International Monetary Fund mission failed to reach agreement with Russia about the next tranche of its loan.

The Russian central bank said in a statement on Thursday a team from the IMF would leave Moscow without reaching a conclusion on whether to give Russia the latest tranche of a three-year $10 billion loan.
"Because of yesterday's news the market is so weak today that small selling was pushing down prices quite noticeably," a Russian bank dealer said.

Dealers said the market was unaffected by news Russia would start presentations on the country's economy to international investors in the week starting November 11 ahead of the long-awaited Eurobond issue.
They said prices had firmed in early Moscow trading but eased afterwards.
"There was no support after Russian buying and it is almost impossible to find somebody who would open new positions now," Eurobank dealer Christopher Ayale said.
He added the downward trend could be also due to year-end squaring of positions in debt instruments, which had already set in.
